rationale: There is a direct conflict in the literature regarding whether missense variants in the MH2 domain of receptor-regulated SMADs accelerate vascular disease and precipitate earlier aortic events compared to truncating/haploinsufficient variants. Functional and cohort findings by de Wagenaar et al. (2024) observed that individuals with dominant-negative MH2 variants experienced more major aortic events (66.7% vs 44.0%) at a younger median age (35.0 vs 46.0 years). Conversely, a systematic cohort and literature evaluation of 155 patients by Chesneau et al. (2020) demonstrated no significant association between variant type (including missense in MH2 vs truncating) and the development of an aortic phenotype (P = .935). In addition, severe infantile aortic aneurysm and early mortality have been documented with truncating loss-of-function mutations (Wischmeijer et al., 2013), further refuting the notion of an exclusive or uniform acceleration driven by MH2 missense alleles.

evidence.text: A cohort analysis of individuals with pathogenic SMAD3 variants demonstrated that individuals with dominant-negative variants in the MH2 domain experienced a higher frequency of major events at an earlier median age compared to those with haploinsufficient variants.

conflicts: Chesneau et al. (2020) demonstrated an explicit lack of correlation between SMAD3 variant type (specifically testing MH2 missense vs truncating variants) and aortic phenotype (P = 0.935) across 155 individuals, contradicting findings of significant genotype-phenotype divergence.

While de Wagenaar et al. (2024) reported earlier major events in dominant-negative MH2 variants (median 35 vs 46 years), the difference only reached borderline statistical significance (P = 0.065), and severe infantile/early adult vascular dissection occurs in families with truncating loss-of-function mutations (Wischmeijer et al., 2013).

new_directions.question_text: Do true dominant-negative SMAD2/3 MH2 variants differ in penetrance or aortic dissection threshold compared to non-dominant-negative missense or haploinsufficient alleles in a standardized prospective registry?
new_directions.rationale: Retrospective literature reviews conflate diverse missense alleles without functional validation of dominant-negative activity, introducing classification bias that could obscure true genotype-phenotype distinctions.

new_directions.question_text: What role do secondary genetic modifiers and TGF-beta pathway transcriptional co-regulators play in modulating the extreme vascular expressivity observed across both truncating and missense SMAD2/3 variants?
new_directions.rationale: Because severe vascular events occur in both infant haploinsufficient patients and older missense carriers, monogenic variant class alone fails to explain vascular progression, suggesting modifier loci.
